Copyright and takedown

How to tell us about content on this site that infringes your rights or is otherwise unlawful, and what happens next.

Last updated 25 September 2026

Contents

  1. Our content
  2. What members upload
  3. Reporting infringement
  4. Counter notices

1. Our content

The reports, text and design on this site belong to Leoside Equity. What you may do with them is set out in section 8 of the terms of service. For permission to go further, write to us.

Reports quote short passages from filings and other published sources for the purpose of commentary and criticism, always with the source named. If you think a quotation goes further than that, send a notice as described below and we will look at it promptly.

2. What members upload

The only thing members can upload is a profile photo. It is visible only to the member who uploaded it. Members confirm, under the terms, that they have the right to use any photo they add.

3. Reporting infringement

If you believe material on this site infringes a copyright you own or are authorised to act for, send a written notice that includes all of the following. These are the elements required by the US Digital Millennium Copyright Act (17 U.S.C. 512(c)(3)), and we accept notices in the same form from anywhere.

  1. Your physical or electronic signature.
  2. Identification of the copyrighted work you say is infringed.
  3. Identification of the material you say infringes it, with the page address, so we can find it.
  4. Your name, postal address, telephone number and email address.
  5. A statement that you believe in good faith that the use is not authorised by the copyright owner, its agent or the law.
  6. A statement that the information in the notice is accurate and, under penalty of perjury, that you are the owner or are authorised to act on the owner's behalf.

When we receive a complete notice we remove or disable the material promptly, tell the member concerned where there is one, and give them a copy of the notice. A notice that knowingly misrepresents infringement can make the sender liable for damages.

4. Counter notices

If material you provided was removed and you believe that was a mistake or a misidentification, you may send a counter notice containing:

  1. Your physical or electronic signature.
  2. Identification of the material removed and where it appeared.
  3. A statement under penalty of perjury that you believe in good faith it was removed by mistake or misidentification.
  4. Your name, address and telephone number, and a statement that you consent to the jurisdiction of the federal district court for your address (or, if you are outside the United States, any judicial district in which Leoside Equity may be found) and will accept service of process from the person who sent the original notice.

We forward counter notices to the original complainant. Unless they tell us within 10 business days that they have filed a court action, we may restore the material within 10 to 14 business days.

5. Repeat infringers

We close the accounts of members who are the subject of repeated valid infringement notices.

6. Other unlawful content

You can report anything else on the site you believe is unlawful the same way. Tell us what it is, where it is, and why you believe it is unlawful, with your name and email address. We review every report, act on it without undue delay, and tell you what we decided. This is also our point of contact under the European Union's Digital Services Act for users and for authorities. We correspond in English.

7. Where to send notices

Our designated agent for notices of claimed infringement, under 17 U.S.C. 512(c)(2), is the Copyright Agent of Leoside Equity. Send notices to support@leosideequity.com with "Copyright notice" or "Illegal content" in the subject. If you need to send a notice by post, write to that address first and we will give you a postal address for service.
